title: Causal Consequence Calibration for Quantized World Action Models
hook: At a matched high-precision-unit budget, the candidate predicts that the rank correlation between local PTQ discrepancy and paired one-step closed-loop consequence will drop specifically on contact-transition states, while consequence-ranked protection will reduce contact-sensitive task failures relative to local-score ranking. The surprising result is the regime split, not a claim that local numerical error is useless everywhere. C_r is not task loss, the physical consequence of executing the full action chunk or a replan horizon, a marginal effect in the jointly low-bit deployment, or a bytes/latency objective; any reduction in held-out task failures is only an empirical predictive test of transfer from this one-control-transition proxy.
hook_shape_rationale: (a) Surprising empirical reveal: the named Spearman rank correlation between local discrepancy and the counterfactual consequence index should be lower on simulator-identified contact transitions, and the same fixed-budget allocation should improve the downstream contact-sensitive task metric. Shape (c) was viable because all allocations use the same precision budget, but it was rejected because the method adds calibration rollouts rather than being strictly no-more-cost on a load-bearing resource.

gap_closure.gap: additive: No retrieved WAM-quantization leaf establishes the downstream consequence of a numerical perturbation at a module or denoising step for the final action chunk and the next closed-loop observation in contact-critical manipulation; this is the unresolved residue of QuantWAMs (arxiv:2607.28405v1), not a request for a particular remedy. — stakes: practitioners may deploy a memory- and latency-efficient WAM that preserves local calibration metrics but fails on contact-sensitive actions, while researchers may mistake local fidelity for transferable closed-loop reliability.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by recasting each numerical intervention as a per-site counterfactual action-and-next-observation consequence functional, then using the companion at the main-pattern level to replace the layer-local fidelity score with a runnable precision-scoring and allocation operator.

gap_closure.gap: subtractive: No retrieved WAM-quantization leaf tests whether the local numerical-fidelity surrogate inherited from layer-local PTQ is actually sufficient for precision selection in the coupled video/action setting, rather than an assumed proxy for downstream task impact; this questions the inherited assumption and leaves the replacement open. — stakes: precision-allocation conclusions can rest on an unexamined surrogate and invalidate comparisons across WAMs or tasks, while deployment teams cannot tell whether an apparent speed or memory gain preserves the action behavior they require.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by evaluating local fidelity and the counterfactual consequence on the same site, history, denoising seed, simulator state, and precision budget, then reporting their divergence separately for contact and non-contact transitions.

core_mechanism: The shared object is a per-site counterfactual consequence index C_r for a numerical quantization site r, where r is a tuple of WAM branch, module, inner denoising step, and weight-or-activation axis; the site registry is enumerated from the public coupled WAM's actual PTQ hooks, so no latent rollout/planning or action-tokenization site is introduced. For calibration episode j, the inputs are the recorded observation history h_j, language instruction l_j, simulator state z_j, denoising seed xi_j, and simulator seed eta_j from an existing RoboTwin 2.0 or LIBERO episode, while F_0 is the full-precision WAM and F_r is the same model with only site r using the matched low-bit numerical quantizer and every other target site left at FP16. Running F_0 and F_r with the same history, seed, cache, and coupled future-video/action inference produces full action chunks a_j0 and a_jr; the first executable action from each chunk is then applied from the identical simulator state z_j to obtain next observations o_(j+1)0 and o_(j+1)r. Define d_a(j,r) as the mean squared difference between the two full action chunks divided by max(sigma_a^2, epsilon_a^2), where sigma_a^2 is the mean coordinate variance of FP16 full action chunks over the calibration episodes and epsilon_a is a named normalized-scale floor; define d_o(j,r) as the mean per-pixel absolute next-observation difference divided by max(sigma_o, epsilon_o), where sigma_o is the calibration mean per-pixel standard deviation. With lambda_a=lambda_o=1 as the default dimensionless weights, selected before held-out evaluation and sensitivity-checked over a named ratio sweep, C_r is the episode mean of lambda_a d_a plus lambda_o d_o, and its top-B sites replace the local PTQ ranking under the same high-precision budget B as the matched baseline. The C00 reframe supplies a computable responsibility-like object and the operator substitution makes it actionable for numerical weight/activation precision selection, while the C02 diagnostic compares C_r with the same-context local discrepancy L_r and uses the simulator's native contact or task-transition flag to report the divergence without treating the evaluated WAM as its own oracle. This closes the additive gap because a single-site perturbation is followed through the coupled action output and an externally simulated next observation, and it closes the subtractive gap because the same paired intervention tests whether L_r is sufficient rather than assuming it. The candidate remains a coupled future-prediction/action-generation WAM method: the minimal Fast-WAM path uses the official released checkpoint in idm mode with sigma_shift_FW=1.0 and the current infer_action path, not first_frame, and numerical W/A quantization only; an optional LingBot-VA replication must use the README's VAE/text-encoder CPU offload and budget backward calibration separately from its reported inference memory. Fake-quant or dequantized GEMM is used only for profiling and must be reported separately from final measurements with the real low-bit kernel. For coherence purposes, C_r is explicitly a single-site FP16-background ranking proxy for one control transition—not the marginal consequence of the jointly low-bit schedule, not a jointly optimality guarantee, not task-success loss, and not a consequence of executing the full chunk or subsequent replanning; the primary allocation budget is B_site, the matched baseline's pre-registered site count, while persistent weight bytes, peak live activation workspace, scale/copy overhead, and latency are separate measured deployment quantities; the concrete method scope is numerical weight or activation intervention inside the coupled future-video/action denoiser with the one-transition estimand and normalized full-chunk/next-observation score, and the broad downstream-task-consequence quantization principle is treated as prior art.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger
P1 — Coupled closed-loop premise: each denoising call produces an action chunk and later calls consume observations affected by earlier actions; this is supported by the WAM formulation and the QuantWAMs pipeline record, but the size of a quantization-induced downstream effect is untested — falsification target.
P2 — Single-site intervention premise: the public WAM/PTQ implementation can execute one named weight or activation site at the matched low-bit setting while the remaining target sites stay at FP16 and the same stochastic state is restored; this is an implementation bet — untested — falsification target.
P3 — External transition premise: RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO provide existing simulator states, action execution, next observations, and native task/contact state needed to compare the two branches without inventing a new large dataset; this is believed true because both are the stated public robot-manipulation evaluation resources.
P4 — Consequence relevance premise: a perturbation that changes the full action chunk and the next simulator observation is more deployment-relevant than a one-call local discrepancy; this follows directly from the Phase 1 bottleneck, but the ranking advantage is untested — falsification target.
P5 — Contact-regime premise: local discrepancy and downstream consequence can rank sites differently around contact or task-state transitions; this is a domain bet motivated by contact-sensitive manipulation, and is untested — falsification target.
observation-model: calibration inputs are sampled as complete episodes from the available RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO splits, not as iid frames; histories are temporally dependent, task and embodiment proportions are inherited from the manifest, and simulator states are selected by the recorded trajectory, so C_r estimates the calibration episode distribution rather than an unbiased deployment distribution. Episode-level resampling and a held-out task/episode split are required.
ESTIMAND: for each site r, C_r estimates the mean dimensionless one-control-transition consequence of intervening on r over the calibration episode distribution D_cal, conditional on the same h_j, l_j, denoising seed xi_j, simulator state z_j, and simulator seed eta_j; it is not an unbiased estimate of global task-success loss or of an arbitrary real-robot deployment population.
lineage constraint: the load-bearing artifact is the paired action-to-simulator-observation counterfactual, not n1 layer-local PTQ, n2 static sensitivity allocation, n3 QuantWM latent rollout/planning, or n4 QuantWAMs joint empirical-Fisher scoring and fixed-count schedule repair.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT (branch (i))
The naive version is runnable-in-principle local PTQ: compute each site's FP16-versus-low-bit local output discrepancy on open-loop calibration inputs and upgrade the top-B sites. It does not already work because it silently assumes that local discrepancy is a sufficient proxy for downstream consequence, and that premise is false in this setting: a changed action chunk changes the next observation and therefore the inputs to later coupled predictions and contact dynamics. The mechanism confronts that failure head-on with paired simulator counterfactuals; ordinary local sensitivity or one-step PTQ does not resolve the WAM-specific combination of coupled video/action denoising, action-mediated state transition, and contact-critical feedback, so this is not a textbook tool application with the structure removed.
BLOCK 3 — design rationale
Both gaps share one intervention registry and one C_r object: the anchor uses it to allocate precision, while the sibling uses the same contexts to isolate whether L_r agrees with it, so no second architecture or dataset is needed. A replay-only local profile in the style of QuantWAMs was rejected because it never executes the changed action to obtain the next observation, and a full Jacobian-product or latent-rollout planner was rejected because it would add unobserved assumptions and move the branch into the excluded latent planning route. The chosen design therefore preserves the WAM's coupled future/action path, adds only a one-site causal diagnostic and matched allocation operator, and explicitly avoids the occupied ancestral nodes and the already-covered QuantWAMs mechanisms. The phrase more deployment-relevant is a conditional design hypothesis rather than an established equality to task loss; no joint-low-bit additivity or single-site-to-joint marginal assumption is made, and the broad downstream-task-consequence principle is prior art.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Freeze the public artifacts and inference contract. Require a pre-existing run-manifest entry checkpoint_FW containing the exact official Fast-WAM released checkpoint filename, repository revision, and immutable digest when available; if the entry is missing or ambiguous, halt before calibration. Set mode_FW=idm, sigma_shift_FW=1.0, and inference_path_FW=infer_action with the README's current no-default-VAE-decoding behavior; do not substitute first_frame because it removes the future branch. Bind b_lo to an exact per-axis numerical weight/activation bit tuple and real low-bit kernel identifier in the same manifest, and halt if the selected real kernel is unavailable; fake-quant/dequantized GEMM is not evidence of kernel support. Keep the action/video coupling unchanged and output a versioned configuration manifest with the checkpoint filename, repository revision, mode, sigma shift, inference path, bit tuple, and kernel identifiers. The minimal validation uses Fast-WAM only; if LingBot-VA is added, use its official VAE/text-encoder CPU-offload inference configuration and report backward-calibration memory as a separate measurement rather than reusing the reported inference-memory figure.
2. Build an episode-level calibration manifest from existing RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO simulator episodes. Set N_cal=32 as the default to match the fixed-trajectory scale reported for QuantWAMs, with a pre-registered 16/32/64 episode sensitivity check; preserve observation histories, instructions, simulator states, action chunks, denoising seeds xi_j, simulator seeds eta_j, and native contact/task-transition flags. For each item, capture a complete paired-state snapshot S_j containing h_j, l_j, simulator state z_j, controller state, simulator RNG state eta_j, model/denoising RNG state xi_j, observation/history buffers, and persistent model-cache state. Output D_cal and a held-out episode/task split without mixing adjacent frames across splits. Reject an empty calibration or held-out split before scoring.
3. Enumerate the intervention registry R from the public WAM implementation. Each r=(branch, module, denoising_step, axis) identifies one actual quantization hook in the coupled video/action denoiser, with axis in {weight, activation}; exclude VAE-only, text-only, latent/action tokenizer, and planner-only sites. Output a deterministic registry with a lexicographic tie-break order and a mapping from each site to its real kernel and exact bit setting. Reject an empty registry before ranking.
4. Measure single-site model interventions with matched stochastic state. For every r and calibration item j, restore an independent clone of S_j before each branch, including controller state, simulator RNG, model RNG/generator, observation/history buffers, and persistent model cache; then run F_0 and F_r with the same h_j, l_j, xi_j, and inference path. Record the full action chunks a_j0 and a_jr and the hook outputs y_jr0 and y_jrr. Define the open-loop local surrogate L_jr as the mean squared difference over all elements of y_jr0 and y_jrr, and L_r as the episode mean of L_jr. Use fake-quant/dequantized GEMM only as a profiling implementation; record whether it was used and keep it separate from the real low-bit-kernel evaluation. Output paired model traces indexed by (j,r).
5. Execute paired environment counterfactuals. Restore independent clones of S_j, including z_j, controller state, simulator RNG eta_j, observation/history buffers, model RNG/generator state, and persistent cache, for the two traces. Apply the first executable action after the restored controller's identical action transformation to each full chunk, and record o_(j+1)0, o_(j+1)r, and the simulator's independent contact/task-transition state. The downstream output of this step is the actual next observation and state transition caused by the altered first action, not merely a changed intermediate discrepancy; C_r therefore does not estimate effects of executing later chunk actions or subsequent replanning.
6. Compute the consequence object. Define sigma_a^2 as the population variance over all scalar coordinates of all FP16 full action chunks in D_cal, and sigma_o as the mean of the population per-pixel standard deviations of FP16 next observations across D_cal. Use named floors epsilon_a=epsilon_o=1e-3 in normalized units, with a pre-registered 1e-4/1e-3/1e-2 sensitivity check. Compute d_a and d_o as the normalized full-action-chunk MSE and next-observation per-pixel L1 differences, set lambda_a=lambda_o=1 by default with a held-out sensitivity sweep over lambda_a/lambda_o in {0.5,1,2}, and output C_r as their episode mean with bootstrap intervals over complete episodes. C_r is a one-control-transition action/observation proxy, not task-success loss.
7. Replace the local allocation operator without retraining. Define B_site, with B equivalent to B_site everywhere in this method, as the nonnegative integer high-precision-site count recorded by the matched local-fidelity baseline in the pre-registered run manifest; halt if that entry is missing or B_site>|R|. Rank sites by C_r and upgrade exactly the top-B_site sites while leaving all other sites at b_lo; resolve ties by the registry order. This primary comparison is a site-count budget only, not a claim of equal bytes or latency. For every schedule, record a separate deployment-cost ledger covering persistent weight bytes including copies and scales, peak live activation workspace under the real kernel, and measured latency; do not substitute that ledger for B_site or call the quantities equivalent.
8. Run the confound-isolating diagnostic. On the same episodes, compare L_r and C_r using Spearman rank correlation separately on simulator-identified contact/task-transition and non-contact subsets, then compare top-B_site C_r allocation against top-B_site L_r allocation and a score-permuted negative control. If fewer than two sites exist, or either score vector is constant in a subset, record Spearman as undefined and skip that correlation rather than fabricate a value. The reported object is the divergence in downstream action/observation and task metrics, not a claim that a correlation itself is causal.
9. Validate the selected schedule on held-out RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO episodes with the real low-bit kernel. Compare FP16, the matched local-fidelity baseline, the C_r allocation, and uniform precision at the same B_site site-count budget; measure task success, contact-sensitive failure rate, full action-chunk deviation, next-observation deviation, peak memory, and latency, with the same Fast-WAM configuration and multiple episode seeds.
10. Keep CPU arithmetic checks and deployment claims separate. CPU runs may verify site indexing, deterministic paired seeds, scale normalization, and C_r arithmetic only; they do not establish robot success, GPU memory, or speedup. Report any LingBot-VA replication as a separate calibration/inference experiment with its offload and checkpoint configuration, and do not combine fake-quant traces with real-kernel performance. Executable branch protocol: the exact Optional IDM checkpoint identity (the checkpoint_FW filename, repository revision, and immutable digest when available) must be present and unambiguous in the pre-run manifest; otherwise halt before calibration. Before either branch, serialize one immutable versioned snapshot S_j in the fixed order controller state, simulator RNG state eta_j, model/generator RNG state xi_j, observation/history buffers, persistent model-cache state, simulator state z_j, and action-transformation state; deep-clone S_j into separate F_0 and F_r copies, restore the complete copy immediately before its branch, and rebuild or invalidate every cache entry whose key or dependency is touched by r before executing that branch. Canonical-serialize and equality-check h_j, l_j, z_j, controller/RNG/history/action-transformation state, and the cache-validity manifest against S_j after each restore; allow only the explicitly recorded r-touched entries to differ after branch-local invalidation/rebuild, abort on any other mismatch, and never share mutable state or cache entries. Equality-check the action-transformation inputs and the first-action mapping before applying each branch's first executable action to its restored simulator, while retaining d_a over the full action chunks, so the first-action environment estimand and full-chunk d_a definition remain unchanged.
falsification_prediction: Run the minimal experiment on the exact Fast-WAM checkpoint_FW in idm mode with sigma_shift_FW=1.0 and infer_action, using a small held-out RoboTwin 2.0/LIBERO manipulation split, the same low-bit setting b_lo, and the same high-precision budget B for local-score and C_r allocations. If the candidate works, the contact-transition subset will show a larger local-score-versus-C_r ranking divergence and the C_r schedule will reduce held-out contact-sensitive task failures and next-observation deviation relative to the matched local-score schedule, without changing the architecture or precision budget. The single load-bearing variable is C_r, the paired downstream consequence index; permute C_r across the site registry before selecting top-B sites, and the predicted effect is that the downstream contact-sensitive success/failure advantage disappears even though the quantizer and evaluation remain unchanged. A positive control is the oracle simulator-state branch that exposes the independent transition outcome during calibration; it should preserve more of the C_r allocation advantage than a model-only local discrepancy if the mechanism, rather than calibration noise, is carrying the result.
compute_budget: 1.2 GPU-day on an 80GB-class equivalent for a staged Fast-WAM-only validation (approximately two short single-GPU A100-40GB stages, no large-model training) + $0 paid API; LingBot-VA replication, if later added, requires a separate calibration-memory and inference budget.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: QuantWAMs already covers joint video/action empirical-Fisher cross terms over block and denoising-step granularity and fixed-count closed-loop protection-schedule repair, so joint coupling, denoising-step sensitivity, closed-loop protection, and contact-critical allocation are prior art; this candidate instead intervenes on one numerical weight-or-activation site r with every other target site at FP16, estimates C_r from paired full action-chunk discrepancy plus the next observation after only the first action is executed, and ranks sites under B_site, without claiming a jointly-low-bit marginal, joint optimality, task-success-loss identity, full-horizon/replan consequence, bytes objective, or latency objective.

QuantWM already covers weight/activation PTQ sensitivity and long-horizon error in a DINO-WM latent planning setting, so latent rollout/planning mismatch and that sensitivity branch are not claimed as novel here; this candidate is a manipulation WAM coupled future-video/action denoiser with a single-site FP16-background numerical intervention, a one-control-transition C_r estimand, and paired full-chunk/next-observation discrepancies rather than a latent rollout/planning marginal or a bytes/latency objective.

VAML is part of the earlier task-consequence/value-aware lineage supplied for this run, so defining a quantization target by downstream consequence is prior art and not this candidate's novelty; the bounded difference here is a single numerical W/A site intervention in a coupled future-video/action WAM, with C_r estimating a one-control-transition paired action/observation proxy and the numerical operator combining normalized full action-chunk MSE with next-observation pixel L1, not a claim of identical objective, task-loss identity, or full-horizon marginal.

Model Advantage / Value-Aware Model Learning is included in the earlier task-consequence lineage, so broad downstream-consequence targeting is prior art; this candidate makes no equivalence claim about objectives or estimands and retains only the narrower concrete intervention of one-site W/A quantization with an FP16 background, the one-control-transition C_r proxy, and top-B_site allocation in a coupled WAM, without joint-low-bit optimality or task-loss claims.

Deep Task-Based Quantization establishes the prior-art principle that downstream task consequence can guide quantization, which is not claimed as novel here; the candidate's distinct bounded object is a single-site W/A PTQ intervention with all other target sites at FP16, C_r over one simulator control transition, and a normalized full-action-chunk plus next-observation numerical score, while held-out task-failure reduction is only a predictive validation of transfer and not C_r itself.

SQIL already treats mission-critical-state protection as prior art through saliency-weighted QAT and action distillation, so protecting contact or other critical states alone is not novel; this candidate uses a different bounded intervention and estimand—single-site numerical W/A PTQ in a coupled future-video/action WAM, paired simulator branches with only the first action executed, and C_r from full-chunk/next-observation discrepancy—and does not claim that SQIL is identical or that critical-state protection alone is its contribution.

Fast-WAM isolates video co-training from explicit future imagination and does not provide a numerical PTQ consequence signal, whereas this candidate keeps the future/action-coupled idm feasibility path and adds single-site weight/activation intervention with consequence-based allocation.

what_step_was_missed: The closest paper would have needed to construct and execute a paired simulator counterfactual in which a single module or denoising-step perturbation changes the action chunk from a fixed state, then measure the resulting next observation or task transition and use that marginal consequence for precision selection; its replayed local discrepancy does not construct this action-mediated transition artifact.
